items.difficulty_reason: For a scheme X and an effective Cartier divisor D in X, the lemma asserts that the map of equation labelled equation-map-effective-Cartier combined with Lemma labelled lemma-compute-for-effective-Cartier defines an isomorphism Li^*K otimes_{O_D} N[-1] -> RSheafHom(O_D, K) functorial in K in D(O_X) (statement lines 3444-3456). Since i_* is exact and fully faithful on modules, it suffices to prove the map is an isomorphism after applying i_*, and the proof uses without further mention the two short exact sequences 0 -> I -> O_X -> i_*O_D -> 0 and 0 -> O_X -> O_X(D) -> i_*N -> 0 from the preceding lemma (proof lines 3458-3468). By Cohomology, Lemma labelled cohomology-lemma-projection-formula-closed-immersion, which defined the map, the left hand side becomes K otimes^L_{O_X} i_*N[-1] = K otimes^L_{O_X} (O_X -> O_X(D)), while the right hand side becomes RSheafHom_{O_X}(i_*O_D, K) = RSheafHom_{O_X}((I -> O_X), K) = RSheafHom_{O_X}((I -> O_X), O_X) otimes^L_{O_X} K, the last equality by Cohomology, Lemma labelled cohomology-lemma-dual-perfect-complex (proof lines 3470-3486). Since the map comes from the isomorphism RSheafHom_{O_X}((I -> O_X), O_X) = (O_X -> O_X(D)), the lemma is clear (proof lines 3486-3490). Reducing to a statement after the fully faithful pushforward and comparing the two two term complexes is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
